parent.description: Config type instance that contains this config child.

username.description: The username used in basic credentials.

password.description: The password used in basic credentials.

secretKey.description: For systems that have a secondary secret key that isn't the password (e.g. Salesforce/CosmosDb)

properties.description:
Other properties for connection configuration. Please note that properties are application specific.

Example: {"readOnly", false} specify the connection in read-only mode.
         {"sslmode", "some-mode"} specify the sssl mode of the connection
         {loginTimeout, 60} specify how long wait for establishment of a database connection in seconds.

secretProperties.description:
Other "secret" properties for connection configuration.

Example: {"password", <myPasswword>} specify the password

url.description: The Url pointing to the database.

certs.description: Tls Certificate if the datastore associated with these credentials needs a secure connection to be accessed

privateKeyAuth.description: Private key authentication for key-pair authentication with the datastore

principal.description: Kerberos principal. Typical format is primary/instance@REALM. (ie. hive/_HOST/PRINCIPAL.COM)

additionalConfigs.description:
This is where you put the additional configurations that're not provided in the basic config.
Note that you can pass any key-value pair as long as it's supported by the service, e.g., to enable kerberos
authentication, ["hadoop.security.authentication", "kerberos"] is necessary.

krbContentOrFileUrl.description:
The Kerberos configuration content for realms and hostnames or url of krb5 realm file.
If this is file url, the url should end with krb5.conf or krb5.ini
If this is krb5.conf content, you can pass as plain text string, and use "\\n" for line breakers.

keytabContent.description:
The user's keytab content that contains encrypted user name and password. As the file is in binary format,
the content needs to be base64 encoded for this field. In Kerberos world, you can login using a principal name
and the password, or, a keytab file that's generated from the principal and the password.

keytabFilePath.description:
The path for the keytab file. If password, keytab content and keytabFile path is given, keytab file path is used.
the keytab content is saved in the file at this location.

pluginId.description:
unique name of a Service Plugin, e.g. cdh5.14.2. If there's no exact match, a plugin will be looked for with
the highest version that matches the given value. e.g. if cdh6 is given, cdh6.3.3 will be resolved.

pluginDir.description: The base directory for this plugin. This directory is always on the local file system.

isDevPlugin.description: During dev, this boolean property will be true.

pluginPaths.description:
classpaths for the plugin

If void, jar files from the plugin directory is tested and used. If there's no such directory for the plugin,
the Java target classes folder and the jar Class-Paths directive are used as the classpaths.
If this field is not null, the list of directories or jar files in the array are used as the classpaths.

database.description: Name of the database going to be connected. (ex: 'my_database_name')

schemaName.description:
For datastores that support it (e.g. currently only snowflake), the schema to be used for accessing tables
in the database.  If not specified then the default schema for the database/user will be used if one exists.
Otherwise, the table schema names should be fully qualified.

driverClassName.description:
Driver class name of the database.  If not provided, this will be inferred from the other parameters.

Ex: 'org.postgresql.Driver' for Postgres.

role.description: Role used when auto-creating the db.

sqlSourceSystem.description:
If not null, the name of the {@link SqlSourceSystem} that created the credentials.  Used to allow verification that
only SqlSourceSystem that created credentials can remove them.

adminDatabase.description: Used to override the default admin db (e.g. "postgres"/"redshift")

adminUsername.description: Used to override the default admin username.

adminPassword.description: Used to override the default admin password.
